metadata.title: Papyrus Known Gaps and Remediation Plan
metadata.remarks: Open items the provider of Papyrus is tracking for the software itself. A deploying organization keeps its own POA&M for its system; these items can be imported into it.

risks.title: AC-2 Account Management
risks.description: A person who holds System Owner through a Papyrus role assignment keeps access while SCIM reports them deprovisioned (intended as break-glass), and there is no administrator action to end a person's active sessions.

remediations.title: Remediate AC-2 Account Management
remediations.description: Limit the SCIM bypass to accounts named in papyrus.yaml and audit each use; add a System Owner action to revoke a person's sessions.

risks.title: AC-3 Access Enforcement
risks.description: Agent sessions, their messages, the AgentFS Library and generated artifacts are owned by the tenant, not by the person who created them. Any signed-in person holding any Papyrus role can list and read every session, Library file and artifact in the deployment.

remediations.title: Remediate AC-3 Access Enforcement
remediations.description: Record an owner on each session and Library namespace, enforce owner or explicit-share checks in the session, workspace-file and artifact routes, and add tests for cross-user denial.

risks.title: AC-4 Information Flow Enforcement
risks.description: Model gateway, identity provider discovery and Sentry connections do not pass the egress gate (they are configured endpoints), and the gate does not pin the resolved address, so a host that changes its DNS answer between check and connect could reach an internal address.

remediations.title: Remediate AC-4 Information Flow Enforcement
remediations.description: Route every outbound connection through the gate and connect to the address that was checked.

risks.title: AC-5 Separation of Duties
risks.description: Action proposals and governed changes do not check that the approver differs from the person who proposed or requested them, so one person holding the approving roles can approve their own request. Unaddressed workflow approval steps can be answered by the run's initiator.

remediations.title: Remediate AC-5 Separation of Duties
remediations.description: Refuse approval when the approver's object ID equals the proposer or requester for action proposals, governed changes and unaddressed workflow steps, with an explicit single-operator override recorded in the audit log.

risks.title: AC-6 Least Privilege
risks.description: Possession of any role, including narrow ones such as Papyrus.Audit.View, grants access to the shared agent workspace: all sessions, chat, Library files and artifacts. Workspace access is not itself a separately assignable privilege.

remediations.title: Remediate AC-6 Least Privilege
remediations.description: Introduce a distinct workspace-use role or per-session ownership (see ac-3) so that narrow roles do not carry workspace access.

risks.title: AC-16 Security and Privacy Attributes
risks.description: Files Papyrus generates (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, exports) are not marked, and records carry no per-item classification.

remediations.title: Remediate AC-16 Security and Privacy Attributes
remediations.description: Stamp the system-high marking on generated files and exports.

risks.title: AU-2 Event Logging
risks.description: Document downloads, session and workflow deletions, and agent tool calls are recorded in their own stores or not at all, rather than in the unified audit trail.

remediations.title: Remediate AU-2 Event Logging
remediations.description: Write these events to the unified audit trail.

risks.title: AU-4 Audit Log Storage Capacity
risks.description: Papyrus does not watch free space on the data volume or alert when it runs low.

remediations.title: Remediate AU-4 Audit Log Storage Capacity
remediations.description: Add capacity monitoring and an alert.

risks.title: AU-9 Protection of Audit Information
risks.description: Triggers detect changes made through the application only; anyone with write access to the database file can rewrite local records, and the unified trail is not hash-chained or signed. Off-host export mitigates this only when configured.

remediations.title: Remediate AU-9 Protection of Audit Information
remediations.description: Chain and sign the unified trail with a key held outside the data directory and verify it on a schedule; require OTLP export on classified deployments.

risks.title: CM-2 Baseline Configuration
risks.description: The baseline is not fully reproducible: base images are referenced by tag rather than digest, apk packages are not version-pinned, and several Python packages in the runtime image (pypdf, pypdfium2, reportlab, pillow) are unpinned.

remediations.title: Remediate CM-2 Baseline Configuration
remediations.description: Pin base images by digest and pin apk and pip package versions, with an automated update process that opens reviewed changes.

risks.title: CM-8 System Component Inventory
risks.description: The SPDX SBOM records name and version only (licenses and download locations are NOASSERTION) and omits OS and Python packages; the image SBOM is not attached to the published image as a signed attestation.

remediations.title: Remediate CM-8 System Component Inventory
remediations.description: Publish the image SBOM as a signed attestation alongside the provenance attestation and include license data.

risks.title: CM-14 Signed Components
risks.description: Signature verification exists only on the Marketplace VM update and image-build paths; the shell updater has no automated test, and other deployment paths do not verify signatures in this repository. The Azure template (deploy/azure/main.bicep) references ghcr.io/beaglabs/papyrus:0.1.1 by tag, a different repository from the one CI publishes (ghcr.io/beaglabs/papyrus/papyrus). Two workflows (container.yml and container-multiarch.yml) sign images for the same repository while the updater trusts only the container.yml identity.

remediations.title: Remediate CM-14 Signed Components
remediations.description: Settle on one signing workflow and identity, reference images by digest from the published repository in every deployment template, add an automated test for the updater verification step, and document signature verification for every supported deployment path.

risks.title: IA-2 Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
risks.description: Papyrus does not itself require multi-factor or certificate-based authentication (it trusts the identity provider's policy) and cannot accept client certificates (CAC/PIV or SIPR tokens) directly.

remediations.title: Remediate IA-2 Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
remediations.description: Optionally require MFA or smart-card authentication methods in the token (amr/acr), and support mutual TLS with NSS PKI where the enclave requires it.

risks.title: RA-5 Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
risks.description: No dependency or static-analysis scanning runs in CI, and there are no severity-based remediation timeframes.

remediations.title: Remediate RA-5 Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
remediations.description: Add dependency and code scanning to CI and publish remediation timeframes.

risks.title: SA-11 Developer Testing and Evaluation
risks.description: Most security tests, including identity, MCP and Key Vault tests, do not run in CI, and the compliance drift check runs only in the local pre-commit hook, which can be skipped. compliance/ssp.md states that these checks run in CI.

remediations.title: Remediate SA-11 Developer Testing and Evaluation
remediations.description: Run the full server test suite and pnpm compliance:check in CI on every pull request and make them required checks.

risks.title: SC-4 Information in Shared System Resources
risks.description: Deleting a session does not remove every copy of its content (workspace files, traces, embeddings), and there is no administrator purge for spillage.

remediations.title: Remediate SC-4 Information in Shared System Resources
remediations.description: Add a cascading purge with verification.

risks.title: SC-5 Denial-of-Service Protection
risks.description: Rate limits are in memory and keyed on the socket address; behind the appliance's nginx proxy every client shares one address, and the limiter clears all windows once it tracks 10,000 keys. The cap of 256 pending sign-ins can be exhausted by unauthenticated requests, blocking sign-in for up to 10 minutes.

remediations.title: Remediate SC-5 Denial-of-Service Protection
remediations.description: Key limits on a trusted forwarded client address, bound memory without clearing all windows, and rate-limit /api/auth/entra/login per client instead of a global cap.

risks.title: SC-7 Boundary Protection
risks.description: The address check resolves DNS separately from the connection that follows, so a host that changes its DNS answer between the two can reach an internal address. The deployment Key Vault is created with public network access enabled.

remediations.title: Remediate SC-7 Boundary Protection
remediations.description: Connect to the address that was checked (pinned lookup) for all outbound requests, and support private endpoints or firewall rules for the deployment Key Vault.

risks.title: SC-12 Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management
risks.description: There is no rotation or key-versioning support for the portal secret or the local master key. Encryption keys for connector credentials are derived with a single SHA-256 of the portal secret, so changing that secret makes stored values unreadable. The Key Vault uses the Standard (software-protected) tier.

remediations.title: Remediate SC-12 Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management
remediations.description: Introduce versioned data-encryption keys with a proper KDF, a re-encryption procedure for rotation, and an option for HSM-backed keys.

risks.title: SC-13 Cryptographic Protection
risks.description: Signatures and MACs use P-256 and SHA-256 rather than the CNSA suite (P-384, SHA-384) that national security systems may require.

remediations.title: Remediate SC-13 Cryptographic Protection
remediations.description: Move Papyrus-generated signatures and MACs to CNSA algorithms while still verifying existing ones.

risks.title: SC-28 Protection of Information at Rest
risks.description: Agent sessions, Library documents, audit records and traces are stored in unencrypted SQLite and AgentFS files; their confidentiality at rest depends on volume encryption the deploying organization provides.

remediations.title: Remediate SC-28 Protection of Information at Rest
remediations.description: Require and verify an encrypted volume for the data directory on classified deployments.

risks.title: SI-2 Flaw Remediation
risks.description: Beag Labs has no documented flaw remediation timeframes by severity, and no published security advisory or vulnerability disclosure process (no SECURITY.md).

remediations.title: Remediate SI-2 Flaw Remediation
remediations.description: Publish a vulnerability disclosure policy and severity-based remediation SLAs, and announce fixed vulnerabilities in release notes.

risks.title: SI-11 Error Handling
risks.description: Unexpected exceptions are returned to the client as 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with the exception's message text, which can disclose internal details.

remediations.title: Remediate SI-11 Error Handling
remediations.description: Return a generic message for unmapped errors and log the detail server-side under the request ID.

risks.title: SR-4 Provenance
risks.description: GitHub Actions are referenced by mutable version tags rather than commit SHAs, and base images and OS and Python packages in the Dockerfile are not pinned, so build inputs are not fully traceable.

remediations.title: Remediate SR-4 Provenance
remediations.description: Pin all Actions to commit SHAs and pin image and package inputs (see cm-2), recording them in the provenance attestation.

risks.title: No third-party assessment or penetration test
risks.description: No 3PAO assessment, independent security assessment or penetration test of Papyrus has been performed. All statements in this file are derived from the source repository and its automated tests.

remediations.title: Remediate No third-party assessment or penetration test
remediations.description: Commission an independent penetration test of the application and appliance, then a 3PAO assessment against the target baseline, and track findings in the POA&M.

risks.title: Controls not verified in an authorized hosting environment
risks.description: Papyrus has not been deployed or assessed within a FedRAMP-authorized or DoD Impact Level authorized boundary, and holds no ATO. The DoD image variant only changes the default Microsoft cloud and embeds the offline license key.

remediations.title: Remediate Controls not verified in an authorized hosting environment
remediations.description: Deploy a reference instance in an authorized environment and verify each control there with a sponsoring agency.

risks.title: Vulnerability scanning and remediation SLAs not formalized
risks.description: CI performs no dependency, static or image vulnerability scanning; there are no severity-based remediation timeframes and no published vulnerability disclosure policy.

remediations.title: Remediate Vulnerability scanning and remediation SLAs not formalized
remediations.description: Add scanning to CI (see ra-5), publish a disclosure policy, and adopt remediation SLAs such as those in the FedRAMP continuous monitoring guidance.

risks.title: Incident response and contingency planning owned by the deploying organization
risks.description: Papyrus ships no incident response plan, contingency plan, or backup tooling. Each deploying organization must cover Papyrus in its own IR and CP documentation, and Beag Labs has no published process for notifying customers of product security incidents.

remediations.title: Remediate Incident response and contingency planning owned by the deploying organization
remediations.description: Publish customer-facing guidance for IR and backup/restore of a Papyrus deployment and a Beag Labs product security incident notification process.

risks.title: Security tests and compliance checks not enforced in CI
risks.description: CI runs type checking and a subset of tests; most security tests and the compliance drift check run only locally through a pre-commit hook that can be bypassed. The generated compliance/ssp.md states that these checks also run in CI.

remediations.title: Remediate Security tests and compliance checks not enforced in CI
remediations.description: Run the full test suite and pnpm compliance:check as required CI checks, and correct the SSP text until they do (see sa-11).

risks.title: License signing-key custody outside assessment scope
risks.description: Licenses are signed offline with Beag Labs' Azure Key Vault keys (beag-master, beag-dev). Custody of and access to those keys is not documented here.

remediations.title: Remediate License signing-key custody outside assessment scope
remediations.description: Produce a control description for the license signing keys, including custody, access and rotation.

risks.title: Agent tool lists do not limit tool use
risks.description: Within an active agent session any tool the deployment offers may be used; the tools listed in an agent's signed revision record intent but are not enforced. Approval prompts, budgets and channel approvals still apply.

remediations.title: Remediate Agent tool lists do not limit tool use
remediations.description: Where an enclave requires per-agent least functionality, restore enforcement of the signed tool list or restrict the deployment-wide tool set.
